analysis:
The changes are confined to the test file provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/EngineV2BridgeTests.swift. Test-only code is not shipped in the provider artifact, so it adds no runtime attack surface. Changed ranges per file_changes: StubTokenizer gains a decodeTable (head lines 146-147, 155); makeBridge gains a stopStringScope parameter passed to EngineV2Bridge (head lines 440, 459); and new tests were added at head lines 844-896, which I only saw as a truncated patch excerpt. That excerpt exercises EngineV2Bridge.matchedStopSequence with ReasoningStopScope. I could not see the production source for matchedStopSequence or the stop-string scope, so I cannot assess its correctness. Those tests only assert benign stop-sequence reporting behavior.

The visible head text also covers the receipt-pump ownership tests (PumpReceiptModel and EngineV2BridgePumpReceiptTests, lines ~248-432) and the SSD cache helpers. These relate to T-041 (prefix cache, scoped cacheSalt, SSD donation, the donation-demand hint, receipt cleanup). They assert that receipts are retained until durable publication, that cancellation retires the receipt without publishing a donor, that cacheScope isolation holds (separate scope-a and scope-b receipts with correct callbacks), and that a demand hint of 0 skips the donation. These tests reinforce rather than weaken the T-041 controls. Base-side units 6 and 7 are existing tests for the L1/L2 tier choice with SSD (corrupt files dropped only when the SSD read is reached), request-id validation, seeded id collision guards, logprobs channel caps, and paged KV capacity; none are changed in a security-relevant way.

No secrets are introduced. Test fixtures use synthetic keys (SymmetricKey random) and temporary directories that are removed on exit. No threat-model assumption is invalidated. The remaining uncertainty is production-side changes to the stop-string scope and matchedStopSequence, which are outside this batch and should be checked in the corresponding source file's review.
